title: ChangeList
description: A list of changes for one Revit model, in flo2-rvt's fixed vocabulary. The agent writes only this data; one reviewed add-in maps each change kind to the Revit API. Version 0 defined the envelope, the element reference and three change kinds; version 1 adds move_levels_together and set_level_elevation's groups_in_the_way. flo2-rvt's edit job runs the changes in order, each in its own transaction, saving the result as a NEW .rvt and never changing the input.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, for editors.

version.description: The change-list format version. A new change kind or field that an older add-in could not read bumps it. Version 1 (flo2-rvt 0.6.0, add-in 0.5.0) adds move_levels_together and set_level_elevation's groups_in_the_way, and a list that uses either says 1; a list of version 0's vocabulary reads as it always did, as version 0 or 1.

list_id.description: An optional id the author gives the list, echoed in the job's report.

description.description: What the list is for, in a sentence or two.

IfcGlobalId.description: An IFC GlobalId: 22 characters of IFC's base-64 alphabet, as Revit's own IFC exporter writes it for the element: the element's IfcGUID parameter when it holds a valid one (never for a curtain wall), otherwise Revit's export id for the element (ExportUtils.GetExportId), compressed. For a level, the GlobalId of the IfcBuildingStorey Revit exports for it.

GlobalIdReference.description: An element named by its IFC GlobalId.

LevelNameReference.description: A level named by its name in the Revit model, matched exactly (case and spaces count).

LevelReference.description: A level, named either by its name or by the GlobalId of the IfcBuildingStorey Revit exports for it.

Length.description: A length with its unit. The add-in converts it to Revit's internal feet (1 ft = 304.8 mm exactly).

ChangeId.description: An optional id for one change, echoed in the job's report next to what Revit did with it.

DeleteElementsOnLevel.description: Delete every model element whose level is this level: its Revit level (Element.LevelId), its base or reference level (a wall's base constraint, a column's base level, a beam's reference level, a stair's or railing's base level, a duct's or pipe's reference level, a group's or a part's base level), or its Schedule Level (a beam's or a face-hosted family's). Elements hosted in them (doors and windows in a deleted wall) are deleted by Revit with their host, and the report names them. Elements that only reach the level from below (a wall or column whose TOP is this level) are kept, as are views, sheets, annotation, links and imports, and the level itself. A member of a group goes with its group, never alone. Everything still tied to the level afterwards is listed in the report with why it was not taken: by its Revit settings, or because Revit's IFC export files it under the level's storey (an element with no level at all, by its height; one on a level that is not a building storey). An element with no level is listed, never deleted.

DeleteElementsByGlobalId.description: Delete the elements named by their IFC GlobalIds. Each must name one model element; a level, a type, a view, a link or a member of a group is refused by name in the report, and a GlobalId that names no element is listed as not found. Revit deletes what is hosted in them with them.

GroupsInTheWay.description: What a level move does when Revit refuses it for a model group in the way ("Changes to groups are allowed only in group edit mode ... You may use the "Ungroup" option"): a group whose type is placed more than once and that the move would change, because its members are tied to levels that move by different amounts, or to one that moves and one that does not. refuse, what a change that says nothing does: the move is rolled back, nothing is ungrouped, and the report names the groups in the way. ungroup: the move is tried first with every group kept; if Revit refuses it for groups in the way and for nothing else, it is tried again with ONLY the group instances Revit named ungrouped (their members stay where they are), in the new model alone. Ungrouped copies are no longer linked to the group type or to its other copies: editing one later does not update the others. The report names every group ungrouped. Say ungroup only once the person has agreed to it. Needs change-list version 1.

SetLevelElevation.description: Set a level's elevation. What is on the level moves with it, as it does in Revit: elements whose base or reference level it is keep their offset from it, elements whose top is constrained to it change height, and hosted elements follow their hosts. Each set_level_elevation runs alone, so what spans this level and one not yet moved is stretched or compressed meanwhile; to shift several levels by one amount, use move_levels_together. A model group in the way is handled as groups_in_the_way says.

relative_to.description: What the elevation is measured from: the project origin (Revit's ProjectElevation), or the level's own Elevation Base setting (Revit's Elevation).

MoveLevelsTogether.description: Move several levels by one vertical offset, together, in ONE transaction: every level named moves by `by`, and Revit regenerates the model once, at the commit, with all of them moved. So what lies between two moved levels keeps its shape and moves whole (a wall from one to the other keeps its height, a stair its rise, a model group spanning them its definition), and only what ties a moved level to one that is not moved changes height (a wall from an unmoved level up to a moved one; the report lists it as top_constrained). Each level is named once, and a move by zero is refused. The report gives each level's elevation before and after, and every message Revit raised. A model group in the way is handled as groups_in_the_way says. Needs change-list version 1.

levels.description: The levels to move, each once, by its name or its storey's GlobalId.

by.description: How far every level moves: up when positive, down when negative, never zero.

Change.description: One change, distinguished by its kind.
